property_summary: After any call to setOwner, the owner state variable must equal the _owner argument passed to the function; the bug sets it to msg.sender instead, breaking this invariant for calls where _owner differs from msg.sender.

Only the admin can change the owner; after any call to setOwner from a non-admin, the owner must remain unchanged. The bugged modifier lets anyone change it, so for some non-admin caller the owner will differ from the original.
A non-admin caller can never change the owner: after any non-admin calls setOwner, the owner remains the same, but the buggy modifier allows anyone to change it.
In the correct contract, only the admin can change 'owner' via setOwner; in the buggy contract, any non-admin caller can change 'owner'.
For any caller that is not the original admin, a call to setOwner must leave the owner unchanged; the bug violates this by allowing any non-admin to change the owner.
The owner can only be changed by the admin; the bug allows any caller to change owner.

For every call to setOwner from the admin, the value of owner must only change to the argument _owner (or remain unchanged if other preconditions fail); the bug violates this by never updating owner while mutating admin.
After setOwner is called by any non-owner address, the owner should remain unchanged in the reference, but the buggy version allows non-admin (any caller) to change the owner.
For any caller that is not the original deployer, calling setOwner must revert; the bug allows a non-deployer to call setOwner successfully by passing the owner check.

For any caller, if setOwner does not revert, the new owner must be the caller; the buggy version can set the owner to an address different from the caller because the modifier checks owner instead of admin.

For any caller, if setOwner succeeds, the new owner must be the caller; the buggy version allows a non-owner caller to set the owner to a different address because the modifier incorrectly checks msg.sender == owner.

For any caller, a successful setOwner in the reference implies the caller was the deployer; in the buggy version, a non-deployer can make setOwner succeed by setting owner to themselves and then calling again, so the rule is violated.
setOwner should succeed and return true when called by the admin, but the buggy version that uses require(false,...) in onlyAdmin always reverts for any caller including the admin.

For any non-admin caller, setOwner must fail with a revert, and the buggy version also reverts for the admin, so the rule must capture that the admin can successfully change the owner while the bug prevents it.
For any caller, if setOwner returns successfully, the owner must have changed to the provided _owner; the buggy version makes setOwner always revert, so it can never successfully change the owner.
